scored_from: only the artifacts saved under docs/termix/evidence/
scorer_note: Same scorer, same rubric, both arms, after execution. Scores are justified per dimension; any dimension that cannot be judged objectively is marked NOT ASSESSABLE.

D1_correctness.justification: 62 selected; 2 adjudicated false positives (MolloW, @cryptohayes) included. Captured all 3 genuine agents Arm B missed.

D2_completeness.justification: Returned matches and raw hit/retrieved counts, but reported no coverage bound in its output shape and no per-record basis.

D3_actionability.justification: Names only; no stable identifier for follow-up. Evidence file shows a 5-name sample without slugs.

D4_data_source_quality.justification: No timestamp, no per-record attribution, no statement of what justified inclusion.

D5_risk_awareness.justification: No limitation or unavailable-metric statement of any kind in the output.

D1_correctness.justification: 58 matched; eliminated 2 false positives BUT missed 3 genuine yield agents via description-precedence. Net correctness comparable to Arm A, not superior.

D2_completeness.justification: Reported matched/retrieved/hits (58/100/131), making coverage bounds explicit and auditable.

D3_actionability.justification: Every record carries a stable registry slug plus chain and verification status.

D4_data_source_quality.justification: Per-record evidenceField, evidenceText, evidenceSource, plus a retrieval timestamp and named source.

D5_risk_awareness.justification: Source framed as inference from metadata (not a registry verdict); category page states unavailable metrics. Not 5 because the false-negative risk of description-precedence is not surfaced to the user.

task-01.verdict: Arm B scored 22/25 vs Arm A 9/25 on the pre-registered rubric. The advantage is in provenance, completeness and actionability — NOT in correctness, where the two arms traded different error types.

D1_correctness.justification: Health-factor category: 7/7 divergent records were false positives. Grid: 3 unguarded matches.

D2_completeness.justification: All four categories reported with hits/retrieved/selected.

D3_actionability.justification: Counts only; no per-record identifier or basis retained.

D5_risk_awareness.justification: No limitation reported; a failure in one category is not distinguished from a genuine zero.

D1_correctness.justification: Eliminated 7/7 health-factor false positives and applied the grid context guard, with no false negatives observed in those two categories. Not 5 because yield-optimisation retains 3 known false negatives.

D2_completeness.justification: All four categories with matched/retrieved/hits and per-record justification availability confirmed true.

D3_actionability.justification: Per-category state plus retrievable justified records; triage decision is directly supportable.

D4_data_source_quality.justification: Explicit state per category, source, timestamps, and evidence retained per record.

D5_risk_awareness.justification: Distinguishes ready/empty/failure states so an upstream failure cannot be misread as zero supply.

task-02.verdict: Arm B 23/25 vs Arm A 8/25. Timing was effectively identical (4159 ms vs 4214 ms) and request cost identical (4 vs 4), so this task shows a QUALITY advantage with NO speed or cost advantage.

D1_correctness.justification: Accepted a challenge selected against mainnet chain 56 — the security-critical failure this task tests. Correctly refused the malformed body.

D2_completeness.justification: Checked object shape and presence of accepts[]/network only; no rail or chain resolution.

D3_actionability.justification: Produces an accept/refuse decision but with a reason that does not support the decision ('network field present').

D4_data_source_quality.justification: Offline by nature; reasons cite only field presence, not a validated rail or chain.

D5_risk_awareness.justification: Explicitly reports chainEnforcement NOT PERFORMED — no chain allowlist exists in the naive procedure.

D1_correctness.justification: Accepted the valid chain-97 challenge, refused the mainnet target, refused the malformed body — 3/3 against the pre-registered success criteria.

D2_completeness.justification: All three cases decided with a specific reason each.

D3_actionability.justification: Decision plus precise reason ('Mainnet (chain 56) is not enabled', 'no payable options').

D4_data_source_quality.justification: Reasons derive from the validated rail/chain resolution. Offline, so no external source to attribute; not 5 for that reason.

D5_risk_awareness.justification: chainEnforcement ENFORCED, and explicitly records signed:false / submitted:false — no transaction risk taken.

task-03.verdict: Arm B 24/25 vs Arm A 7/25. This is the strongest and least ambiguous result: Arm A ACCEPTED a mainnet-targeted payment challenge that Arm B refused.

timing_summary.task-01: Arm A 5513 ms vs Arm B 1426 ms (single run, warm network)
timing_summary.task-02: Arm A 4214 ms vs Arm B 4159 ms (no meaningful difference)
timing_summary.task-03: Arm A 0 ms vs Arm B 2 ms (both effectively instant; Arm B is 2 ms slower)

cost_summary.billable_upstream_requests: task-01 1v1, task-02 4v4, task-03 0v0 — identical in every task
cost_summary.monetary: NOT MEASURABLE — no published per-request price

honest_caveats: Timings are single-run, not averaged; task-01's gap is influenced by network variance and cannot be attributed solely to the agent.
Arm A is a scripted naive baseline, not a skilled human analyst; a skilled analyst would likely score higher on correctness.
No cost advantage was demonstrated in any task.
Arm B has 3 known false negatives in yield-optimisation.
